title: Twin Earth NYC World Model Proposal
description: A proposal is a speculative request to change the world state. Before any significant change is applied to the canonical world, it goes through the proposal pipeline: creation, constraint checking, simulation, review, and commit/reject. Proposals carry an intent (what the change is trying to achieve), the constraints that were evaluated, the assets affected, a confidence score, rollback instructions, and the detailed list of proposed changes. The proposal system is the gatekeeper of world consistency — it prevents impossible, contradictory, or balance-breaking changes from being applied.

proposal_id.description: Globally unique proposal identifier. Format: PROP_{hex-hash}. Example: PROP_e7a3b1c0.

intent.description: Human-readable description of what this proposal intends to accomplish. Written as a declarative goal statement. Examples: 'Damage facade of building at 412 W 42nd after player explosion', 'Spawn portal in Central Park responding to artifact activation', 'Transition traffic signal to emergency mode for police pursuit'.

intent_category.description: Category of the intended change. 'composite' for proposals that bundle multiple change types.

subsystem.description: Subsystem that generated this proposal. Examples: 'player_action_handler', 'npc_ai', 'portal_manager', 'heat_engine', 'narrative_engine', 'world_model_ai'.

trigger_event_id.description: Event ID that triggered this proposal, if any.

trigger_message_id.description: Event bus message ID that triggered this proposal, if any.

constraint_name.description: Name of the constraint that was evaluated. Examples: 'physics_plausibility', 'material_compatibility', 'heat_budget', 'entity_exists', 'position_valid', 'portal_stability_sufficient', 'authority_permission', 'narrative_consistency', 'lod_budget', 'performance_budget'.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this constraint checks.

result.description: 'pass' = constraint satisfied. 'warn' = constraint marginally satisfied, proceed with caution. 'fail' = constraint violated, proposal should be rejected.

detail.description: Explanation of the constraint evaluation result. For failures: what went wrong. For warnings: what is marginal.

severity.description: 'advisory' = a failure is a recommendation, not a hard block. 'blocking' = a failure prevents the proposal from being accepted.

constraints_used.description: All constraints evaluated against this proposal, with their results. A proposal with any blocking failures cannot be accepted.

assets_affected.description: Entity IDs of all entities that would be modified, created, or destroyed by this proposal. Used for conflict detection — two proposals affecting the same entity cannot be committed simultaneously without resolution.

regions_affected.description: Region names affected by this proposal. Used for spatial conflict detection and heat impact routing.

confidence.description: Proposer's confidence that this change is correct, appropriate, and will not cause unintended consequences. 0 = blind guess. 1 = mathematically certain. Low-confidence proposals receive more scrutiny and may require simulation. AI-generated proposals typically range 0.6-0.9. Player-action-derived proposals are typically 0.95+.

strategy.description: 'inverse_changes' = apply the reverse of each proposed change. 'snapshot_restore' = restore from a world state snapshot. 'event_replay' = replay events from a checkpoint, skipping this proposal. 'manual' = requires human/designer intervention to undo. 'irreversible' = cannot be rolled back (e.g., NPC death in a no-respawn universe).

snapshot_ref.description: Reference to the pre-proposal snapshot, if snapshot_restore strategy.

inverse_changes.description: Explicit inverse operations for inverse_changes strategy.

estimated_rollback_time_ms.description: Estimated time to complete rollback in milliseconds.

rollback_path.description: Instructions for undoing this proposal if it needs to be rolled back after commitment.

audit_note.description: Freeform note for the audit trail. Explains reasoning, edge cases considered, or designer override justification. Persists permanently for post-mortem analysis.

entity_id.description: Entity ID being modified. For spawn operations, this is the new entity's ID.

operation.description: 'modify' = change a field on an existing entity. 'create' = spawn a new entity. 'delete' = remove an entity.

field.description: Dot-notation path to the field being changed. Example: 'position.x', 'state.operational_mode', 'components.npc.stress_level'. For 'create' operations, this is 'entity' (the entire entity). For 'delete', this is 'entity'.

old_value.description: Current value of the field before the change. Null for 'create' operations. Used for conflict detection — if the actual current value differs from old_value, the proposal is stale and must be re-evaluated.

new_value.description: Proposed new value for the field. Null for 'delete' operations. Type must match the field's schema definition.

change_reason.description: Why this specific field change is needed. Example: 'Explosion blast radius reached this facade panel', 'Portal stability dropped below threshold'.

proposed_changes.description: The atomic list of changes this proposal applies. Each change targets one field on one entity. Changes are applied atomically — all succeed or all fail.

status.description: 'pending' = awaiting evaluation. 'simulating' = running in a sandbox branch to predict outcomes. 'accepted' = passed all constraints and simulation, ready to commit. 'rejected' = failed constraints or simulation, will not be applied. 'committed' = applied to the canonical world state.

status_history.description: History of status transitions for auditability.

simulation_results.description: Results from running this proposal in the simulation sandbox. Populated when status transitions from 'simulating' to 'accepted' or 'rejected'.

simulation_branch_id.description: World state branch ID used for the simulation.

simulation_duration_ms.description: How long the simulation ran in milliseconds.

simulated_time_span_s.description: How much simulation time was covered in seconds.

heat_delta.description: Predicted heat impact from the simulation.

entities_affected_count.description: Number of entities that changed state during the simulation.

cascade_events_count.description: Number of follow-on events triggered by the proposed change during simulation.

npc_panic_count.description: Number of NPCs that entered panic state during simulation.

authority_responses_triggered.description: Types of authority responses triggered during simulation.

frame_time_delta_ms.description: Estimated frame time impact in milliseconds.

entity_count_delta.description: Net change in active entity count.

narrative_flags_set.description: Narrative flags that would be set by this proposal's consequences.

risk_score.description: Overall risk score from the simulation. 0 = safe, predictable outcome. 1 = extremely risky, chaotic consequences. Proposals above the risk threshold require reviewer override.

metrics.description: Quantitative metrics from the simulation run.

side_effects.description: Unintended side effects discovered during simulation.

recommendation.description: Simulation engine's recommendation for this proposal.

modification_suggestions.description: Suggested modifications if the recommendation is 'accept_with_modifications'.

reviewer_type.description: Who/what reviewed this proposal. 'automatic' = passed all constraints with no simulation needed. 'ai_reviewer' = reviewed by a world model AI. 'designer' = manually reviewed by a human designer. 'player_vote' = community voted (for user-generated content).

reviewer.description: Review information. Populated when a proposal requires or receives explicit review.

priority.description: Processing priority. Critical proposals (e.g., portal collapse) skip the simulation queue.

depends_on.description: Proposal IDs that must be committed before this proposal can be applied. Used for ordered dependency chains.

conflicts_with.description: Proposal IDs that conflict with this one (cannot both be committed). Used for mutual exclusion.

committed_at.description: When this proposal was committed to the world state. Null if not yet committed.

ttl_ms.description: Time-to-live for this proposal in milliseconds. If not committed or rejected within this window, the proposal expires and is auto-rejected. Prevents stale proposals from clogging the pipeline.
